answer: 36.0% of the 175 assayed miRNAs (63 of 175) show significant differential expression between patient and control groups before multiple testing correction. Specifically: an unpaired two-sample Welch t-test on the raw mean-of-triplicate Ct values (patients P_1–P_10 vs controls C_11–C_20, observed non-missing values per miRNA, pairwise complete) yields p < 0.05 for 63 miRNAs — i.e., 63/175 × 100 = 36.0% (denominator = all 175 assayed miRNAs in the table). No multiple-testing correction was applied. Supporting sensitivity checks: Wilcoxon rank-sum gives 59/175 (33.7%); Welch restricted to the 161 fully-observed rows gives 59/161 (36.6%); imputing the 22 blank cells as Ct=40 gives 61/175 (34.9%) — all consistent with the primary estimate.
